themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK, a 357% increase over the 8-week average of 0.9 weekly complaints, signaling a potential emerging quality-of-life issue in Sunnyside/Woodside recreational spaces.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike, z-score: 4.0)
High statistical significance indicates this is not random variation but a genuine emerging pattern
No prior Reddit or media coverage of park noise issues in the district
reporting_angles: Which parks are affected and what type of noise (music, gatherings, construction)?
Interview residents and Parks Dept. to understand what triggered the spike this specific week

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 5 complaints last week, a 700% spike from the 8-week average of 0.6, suggesting mounting friction over restaurant sidewalk operations or expansion in the district.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 3.32)
Coincides with spring/summer season when outdoor dining typically expands
Streetsblog coverage of bike boulevard planning (May 13) suggests active street-use policy conversations in area
reporting_angles: Are restaurants expanding sheds/seating without proper permits or community approval?
Are complaints about obstruction, noise, or sanitation from specific establishments?

themes_detail.label: Tree & Vegetation Health Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about overgrown tree branches and dead/dying trees combined reached 8 complaints last week (5 + 3), a 280% aggregate spike from the baseline, suggesting neglected street tree maintenance across Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: Overgrown Tree/Branches: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (186% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Combined signal suggests systemic Parks Dept. maintenance backlog in the district
reporting_angles: Inspect Parks Dept. street tree trimming and removal schedules for CD 402
Interview residents about visible tree hazards (low branches blocking sightlines, dead limbs over streets)

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 5 last week, a 233% increase from the 8-week average of 1.5 weekly complaints, raising public health and sanitation concerns.
evidence: 5 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% increase, z-score: 4.95)
High statistical significance (z-score 4.95) rules out random variation
May indicate wildlife issues, unsanitary conditions, or delayed removal by Sanitation Dept.
reporting_angles: What type of animals (rats, pigeons, larger wildlife) and where concentrated?
Check Sanitation Dept. response times for carcass removal in the district

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints jumped to 17 last week, a 143% increase from the 7.0 weekly baseline, indicating accelerating issues with building and infrastructure upkeep.
evidence: 17 Maintenance/Facility complaints last week vs. 7.0 weekly average (143% spike, z-score: 3.43)
Broad category—requires drill-down to identify specific complaint types (subway stations, public buildings, streetscape?)
No corroborating Reddit or community board data yet
reporting_angles: Disaggregate 311 data to learn whether complaints target MTA facilities, city buildings, or general streetscape
Interview NYC311 or relevant agency to understand maintenance backlog in CD 402
